To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
small molecules that bind stem-loop I of an RNA replication control element can induce loss of an IncB-type plasmid in vivo.

small molecules that bind RNA can be used to mimic plasmid inactivation in vivo, and that aminoglycides with the ability to bind RNA are more likely to induce plasmids loss than are compounds without RNA binding ability.
aminoglyco-sides that bind to a specific RNA element of an IncB replicon are able to induce the plasmid loss phenomenon in vitro and in vivo.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of small molecules that target RNA and that can be used to induce the loss of plasmids from bacteria.
the discovery and development of small molecule antibiotics that can eliminate the plasmids that cause bacterial resistance to traditional antibiotics.
the development of small molecules that can induce plasmid elimination from bacteria and the subsequent resensation of bacteria to antibiotics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
aminoglycides that bind to RNA stem loop I of the IncB plasmids cause plasmid loss from E. coli.
aminogly-cosides that bind to SLI are capable of inducing plasmid loss, whereas aminoglyco-sides that do not bind SLI are incapable of inducing plasmids loss.
the binding affinity of aminoglycides to the SLI region of the IncB RNA replication control element is a key determinant of the plasmid inactivating effect of these compounds.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the RNA binding properties of aminoglycides can be used to predict their plasmid inactivation properties.
the RNA binding proclivities of aminogly-cosides can be used to predict their antiplasmic activity.
we have identified a small molecule that can induce plasmid inactivation and resensitize bacteria to antibiotics by targeting RNA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
RNA can be used to control plasmid replication and, in doing so, can be used to eliminate plasmids and resensitize bacteria to antibiotics.
RNA is a viable target for the treatment of plasmid-based infections.
the RNA binding proclivities of aminoglyco-sides can be used to predict their ability to induce plasmids loss and resensitize bacteria to antibiotics.
